turns.user: The pull subscription sub-billing-export on gxdr-prj-core-prd is gone, and Terraform wants to recreate it. The Globex Drill Systems data team paused their consumer in August. What happened?

input.command: gcloud pubsub subscriptions describe sub-billing-export --project gxdr-prj-core-prd

turns.assistant: Pub/Sub deleted it. A subscription with no `expiration_policy` gets the default one: it is deleted after 31 days without subscriber activity, and a paused consumer counts as inactive. On `google_pubsub_subscription`, set `expiration_policy { ttl = "" }` so it never expires; any other ttl only moves the deadline. The recreated subscription starts with an empty backlog, so messages published while it was gone are lost to it.

turns.result: The file pubsub.tf has been updated.

turns.user: We enabled uniform bucket-level access on the logs bucket. Can we go back if a legacy ACL consumer breaks?

turns.assistant: Yes, but only for 90 days: once uniform bucket-level access is enabled you can disable it until the `lockedTime` shown (90 days after enabling); after that it is locked on permanently. Object ACLs are ignored while it is on, so test every legacy ACL consumer inside that window.

turns.user: The staging Cloud SQL instance got deleted from the console even though Terraform shows deletion_protection = true. How?

turns.assistant: Two different switches. `deletion_protection` on `google_sql_database_instance` is Terraform-only: it blocks `terraform destroy` and replacements, nothing else. `settings.deletion_protection_enabled` is the API-level flag that also blocks deletion from the console and gcloud. The instance was deleted in the console, so only `deletion_protection_enabled = true` would have stopped it. Set both on stateful instances.

turns.result: The file sql.tf has been updated.

turns.user: The Artifact Registry repo is huge. Add cleanup policies, but I'm scared of deleting prod images.

turns.assistant: Start with `cleanup_policy_dry_run = true` on `google_artifact_registry_repository`: the policies are evaluated and every would-be deletion is logged, but nothing is deleted. Review those log entries for a week, then set it to false to enforce.
